title: Number of Equivalent Domino Pairs
summary: Count the number of distinct pairs of dominoes from a list where each pair can be made identical by rotating one of the dominoes.
statement: Count the number of distinct pairs of dominoes from a list where each pair can be made identical by rotating one of the dominoes. Each domino is represented as a pair of integers [a, b], and two dominoes are considered equivalent if they match either as is or when one is rotated.
constraints: Count index pairs of equivalent dominoes.
hints: Normalize each domino to its sorted endpoint pair.
A group of count c contributes c(c-1)/2 index pairs.
Normalization captures reversal equivalence and the combination formula counts every unordered pair once.
editorial: Normalization captures reversal equivalence and the combination formula counts every unordered pair once.

tests.explanation: The first two dominoes form the only equivalent pair.
Three copies of 1,2 create three pairs.
